We present a logical relations for a probabilistic programming with continuous random variables, and with a scoring operator for expressing observations and constraints, and we prove it sound for contextual equivalence.

(a) we have developed a logical relation that proves contextual equivalence for a probabilistic programming with a scoring operation, (b) our logical relation is sound with respect to the operational semantics, and (c) our logical relation has been used to prove several useful equivalences, including re-ordering, which is sound for the effects of sampling and scoring but not for effects that modify state.

the development of a logical relation for probabilistic programs with continuous random variables.
